info.title: Secret Sources API
info.description: Pull host passwords and keys from 1Password, Bitwarden, Infisical, HashiCorp Vault, KeePass, AWS, Azure or Google Cloud when you connect instead of storing them in Termix.

bearerAuth.description: Session token sent in the Authorization header as Bearer and the token.

cookieAuth.name: jwt
cookieAuth.description: Session JWT cookie set at sign-in. When present, it takes precedence over the Authorization header.

apiKeyAuth.description: API key sent in the Authorization header as Bearer and the key, which starts with tmx_. It acts as the key owner and cannot act as anyone else.

get.summary: List secret sources visible to the caller (own + shared)

post.description: kind is onepassword-connect, infisical, bitwarden-sm, hashicorp-vault or bitwarden-cli. Sharing a source with every user requires admin. The token (JSON for kinds with several fields) is stored encrypted on the server and never returned.

put.summary: Update a secret source (owner only; omit token to keep it)

post.summary: Check that a secret reference resolves, without returning the secret
post.description: Uses the same source a connection would use. Answers 200 with a status of found, invalid, no_source, not_found, denied or connection.

post.summary: Check that the source is reachable and the token is accepted

get.summary: Items to pick from a secret source
get.description: Lists items of a source you own or that is shared with you, as references to fill a username and password. Never returns a secret value. Only some kinds of source can list items.

400.description: This kind of source can't list items.

502.description: The source could not be reached.

get.summary: Whether the caller's own vault for this source is unlocked

200.description: unlocked, the account email, how it was unlocked and when it locks again.

400.description: This source is not unlocked per user.

post.summary: Unlock the caller's own vault for this source
post.description: method is password (email, password, optional twoFactorProvider and twoFactorCode), apikey (clientId, clientSecret, password) or sso (redirect, the address the SSO window ended on, and password). password is always the master password. The vault stays unlocked for the caller only, until the source's session length runs out.

400.description: Sign in failed. twoFactor lists the two-step login providers when a code is needed.

delete.summary: Lock the caller's own vault for this source

400.description: This source is not unlocked per user.

post.summary: Start an SSO sign in to the caller's own vault
post.description: Returns the address to open. The sign in ends on a localhost address, which the caller pastes back to the unlock route with their master password.

400.description: This source is not unlocked per user.
